usageNotes: Use this to modify the configuration of an existing LXC container — CPU, memory, network interfaces, mount points, tags, hostname, and more — without recreating it. The call returns null synchronously (no UPID); most settings take effect on the next container start, but some (like description and tags) apply immediately. Requires at least one of VM.Config.Disk, VM.Config.CPU, VM.Config.Memory, VM.Config.Network, or VM.Config.Options on /vms/{vmid}; non-volume bind-mount points are restricted to root@pam.

examples.summary: Increase memory to 2 GB and add a tag for a running web container

params.description: Nginx reverse proxy for client portal

tips: Pass the 'digest' field (from GET config) to guard against concurrent edits — the API rejects the update if the config has changed since you read it.
Use the 'delete' param to unset optional fields (e.g., delete='nameserver,searchdomain') rather than sending empty strings.
Changing 'unprivileged' after container creation is unsupported and can break filesystem permissions — treat it as read-only post-create.
Network interface changes (net[n]) take effect on the next container start; the running container keeps its current network state.
The 'revert' param discards a pending (unapplied) config change without requiring a full reconfigure cycle.
